newsitem.title: UK: Germany sells first chunk of oil reserves - trade.
newsitem.headline: Germany sells first chunk of oil reserves - trade.

text.p: Germany on Tuesday sold the first tranche of crude oil from its strategic reserves to plug holes in government finances and help meet the criteria for European economic and monetary union.
The Hamburg oil supply agency EBV sold all 450,000 cubic metres, or 2.8 million barrels of high sulphur (sour) crude offered in the first of a series of tenders, industry sources said.
"Everything was sold," said a senior trader for a German oil company.
Details of the successful bidders and prices paid were not immediately available.
The crude -- typically a mixture of Iranian Heavy, Saudi Light and Iraqi Kirkuk -- had been pumped from salt caverns via a pipeline to storage tanks at the northern port of Wilhelmshaven.
Tender winners have between Wednesday and the end of August to lift the crude oil. A second sale could follow in September, trading sources said.
Earlier this summer Bonn said it hoped to raise 400 million marks ($215 million) this year and 500 million marks in 1998 by selling oil stockpiled since the late 1970s.
The government plans to sell more than 50 million barrels of crude in total or about 20 percent of national strategic reserves.
Oil traders said some bidders were put off by the way the tender was arranged.
Bids had to be submitted in German and on the basis of marks per cubic metre, unusual for a market which usually deals in dollars per barrel or tonne.
